## Design

### 2026-11-01: The first hour consisted of researching parts and listing everything needed. (Research.md, Requirements.md, and BOM.md)

**10h**

The first hour consisted of researching parts and listing everything needed. (Research.md, Requirements.md, and BOM.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/47e5e4c62cf9dca8694c8e0570ea24e98f1fced361780313a774e611c085a7fa.png)

In hour 2, Mapped out the hardware bus layout. I placed the digitizer and SD card reader on a shared secondary SPI bus (HSPI) with separate chip selects. Calculated memory requirements: a 648x480 1-bit framebuffer requires only 38.8 KB of RAM, meaning the ESP32-S3's 512 KB internal SRAM and 8 MB PSRAM provide plenty of room for multiple buffers and history undo stacks. (Architecture.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/d58bb183eff4980d485bf6de896afb5dd7c552505324f0bcc67f6c7f74968d8b.png)

In hour 3, I built the electrical power tree schematic. Connected an 1800 mAh LiPo cell to a TP4056 USB-C charging IC paired with a DW01A protection IC to prevent over-discharge below 3.0V. (Electrical.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/c5bc7ec2a9066282efbdca776f47a5d6674ca15e46bc92b32943523921b0c689.png)

 In hour 4, I drafted the complete GPIO routing table for the ESP32-S3. Avoided known strapping pins (GPIO0, GPIO45, GPIO46) that could accidentally force the board into bootloader mode on startup. (Pinmap.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/3c604a00af5afb765516d347c6ef5cb439d865329396b5f062618aa9bf7a7cec.png)

In hour 5, I mapped out the UC8179 command sequences. Documented the full global refresh sequence (3.5 seconds, clears ghosting) versus the partial refresh sequence (300 ms window updates for typing and pen strokes). (Display_Digitizer.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/2e13cf0e6a96a476fa008c5b4496dcea596524568795efb06e5b65ebc3826e8e.png)

In hour 6, I created the bridge between the raw digitizer coordinates and the actual display pixels. (Calibration.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/b2a6ffb5124d5c0e0fc23932452ed7b5ad54326c1a5dec4925cb45717a0916c1.png)

In hour 7,  I built the system power state model. Active drawing pulls roughly 38 mA, giving 45+ hours of continuous note-taking from the 1800 mAh cell. (Power.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/10360bda7ba4998be1484b6fcf5fdb1d840b47cfc6a9a5e0e226ed88b385f6c3.png)

In hour 8, I designed the custom E-Paper Graphic binary vector format. Each file begins with a compact 16-byte header containing file signature, timestamp, resolution, and total stroke count. (Storage.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/ab9f28df0fbf497f5b3539e83876dcc5f70bccaf82c9a6ed378cef30195c862c.png)

In hour 9, I built the UI by placing a thin 32-pixel utility toolbar along the top edge featuring Pen, Eraser, Clear Screen, Page Navigation, and Battery indicators. Defined palm-rejection logic: whenever the stylus tip touches the screen, the system ignores peripheral edge contacts to prevent accidental button presses. (UI.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/b00248b477a94b581900325aee3b1f7688a7dca0809059e131c06bd2d63da226.png)

In hour 10, I wrote a hardware assembly guide for when I build it. It covers battery connector polarity checks, FPC ribbon cable insertion, component placement inside the 3D-printed frame, and first-boot smoke testing using a current-limited bench supply or USB monitor. (Assembly.md)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/365206fa8b4095288933e5921aa2f6bd6922a5b077ba6f04373d661f725c93ea.png)

### 2026-11-01: Hour 1: Initialized the PlatformIO project with ESP-IDF and Arduino frameworks. Split duties between the two Xtensa CPU cores using FreeRTOS. Core 0 runs the time-sensitive input polling task (200 Hz)

**9.5h**

Hour 1: Initialized the PlatformIO project with ESP-IDF and Arduino frameworks. Split duties between the two Xtensa CPU cores using FreeRTOS. Core 0 runs the time-sensitive input polling task (200 Hz), while Core 1 handles rasterization, storage, and screen updates. Connected the tasks via FreeRTOS thread-safe queues.   (Input .cpp & .h, platformio.ini)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/2378007764c345c96beca9f46ee902f70b291dd600946c9a272e73b8fce4636d.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/7ad9a74f368b9f1c99fd86ea3a69ac56ae7213b4e43884ed079ae2b185379a39.png)

Hours 2-3: Implemented the display driver with high-speed 10 MHz SPI commands. Allocated the 38.8 KB 1-bit framebuffer in memory. Built the display_update_partial() routine, which sends window coordinate commands (PTL, PTIN) to refresh only the bounding box where ink was drawn, avoiding full-screen flash during active writing. (Display .h &.cpp)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/544f81bae13393e4dda0d3c68480a63a854a1a7105623b493770995f795843ab.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/2c4b92bb51fb905778320d9d6642a61290608f208f720e313d5823cbc66cda0e.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/f7b705190882bc0f44339911b80999a75794fbc853cf936d25c0147260dad7aa.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/2980e5aa4efb4eebd78674e06b1b796d819aee18df305bd30e0fef40c1d0c541.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/d0b0004642b7f0b3ed799ef348af0c021ec1c012c21c803b064b47341ab741f7.png)

Hour 4-5: Calibration software. I added an interrupt handler connected to the digitizer's touch pin. When touched, the driver reads raw X/Y coordinates over SPI, runs them through the 6-parameter affine transformation matrix, and drops calibrated screen coordinates into the input queue. Integrated NVS read/write routines to keep calibration intact across power cycles. (Digitizer, calibration .h & .cpp)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/f16d111872b5500c5039fd7073c7bc44cfe0da1acf4aa438863be18804aae0cd.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/e66e5eafddb53fca13eeca5e58fb66bb07709aa387a2f7c2946886ff27f10783.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/d0686e4abca89bc09354ea9e84bb0d58ea8eb78a97a011501eeaee9294ffefd1.png)

Hour 5-6.5: Added storage and autosave. Implemented the MicroSD storage driver using the FAT32 filesystem over SPI. Built an asynchronous auto-save task that runs every 30 seconds. When changes are detected, it flushes the current in-memory vector stroke list into an .epg file on the SD card while giving CPU priority to pen input. (storage .h and .cpp)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/7c782e5958d4700c5ca99a75d46080cb0b23078ddb8d526d6752de888eecae96.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/599959def5446fa2267399844dc5405ad46190fe50a11b5243dabaad97d30de0.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/0a39b73f79fcdb465656bdabde2c4cafe53c44465ee2728656ebc47471dc86f5.png)

Hour 6.5-8: Coded more of the UI rendering module for the top bar (tool switching, clear canvas, page next/prev). Added battery voltage sampling using the ESP32-S3's internal ADC with voltage-divider calibration to calculate battery percentage. Implemented the auto-sleep timer that puts the chip into deep sleep when no input has occurred for 3 minutes. (ui and power .h & .cpp)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/e3bcc58e1b6d37115319ad6fadbe80a6903778b7f406f7310928e2e1eba5f6cd.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/16dbf9e670da15926b5d267510ffecc83b483065ef74d1381b4c8f88e64ed014.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/13d7a89b25be25151a8a3f4aca855a97531d952b2c14d26d50688021b1ee1d4f.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fpT4vKaaCxCaCu9yi3OynxGXkAPlXNzI/52d2d3b74e1bb4cdcc8bc6e3c9d60019741b5e94e807e92832751050dc381922.png)

Hour 8-9.5: Finishing touches. Added a lightweight Wi-Fi HTTP file server allowing users to view and download their notes from a browser. Created an interactive serial CLI (diag_cli.cpp) for testing hardware buses and checking battery voltage. Assembled a self-contained, single-file Arduino sketch (supreme_display.ino) for quick flashing, wrapping up the full 20-hour engineering sprint. (Sync, diag_cli, ,aom .h and .cpp as well as supreme_display.ino)
